note: RoboARC release record (docs/benchmarks/roboarc.md), written by tools/release/release_rebuild.py --onto. release_commit: the simulator commit the image, the tooling and the instances come from; runtime: the image's installed runtime; bases: one record per task base (ported_from / template, instance, facts the texts state, evidence). version: the task set's version (the Release line of every task README; the image's version is images/roboarc/VERSION); changes: Change Log entries of every base.

changes.text: RoboARC 1.0.1, texts and the monitor's image reference only: the texts, comments and docstrings of this task cite this repository's paths (docs/PROTOCOL.md, docs/STANDARD_MODE.md, docs/TAXONOMY.md, tools/release/release_rebuild.py, images/roboarc/) and carry no internal notes, `[task].name` is `roboarc/<dir>` (it was `robot-coding-bench/<dir>`), and the Release line names the task set's version (the image stays `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.0.0`). The resource-monitor sidecar runs RoboARC's own build of its image, `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc-monitor:0.1.0` (images/monitor/; the same files and command as the earlier `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/efe:monitor-0.1.0`). The instruction, the logic of the grader and of the sim service, the tooling, the runtime binding, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.0.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, the image without Genesis: `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.1.0` is built from the Python base image with the same operating system, the same Debian package versions and the same wheels (by sha256) as 1.0.0, without genesis-world, libuipc and the packages only they used (no task of 1.0.0 ran on them: every base is MuJoCo, every family renders with nyx_direct.py). The simulator source drops its Genesis-only modules, the tooling (v20) drops the libuipc build choice and Genesis' kernel replacements, so the runtime binding names the new simulator source, tooling and runtime. The instruction, the grader, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged; every reference replays in the new image to the end state it reaches in 1.0.0: results graded under 1.0.x stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, every image by digest: the Dockerfiles and compose files name the simulator image and the resource monitor's image by manifest digest, `ghcr.io/embodied-first-exam/roboarc:1.1.0@sha256:85ea9003…` (images/pins.json), so a pull gets exactly the image that was validated (until now the simulator image was named by its tag). The image, the instruction, the grader, the tooling, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.1.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.1.0, the agent container's client packages are installed from a hashed lock: `environment/client-requirements.txt` keeps the same versions and adds the sha256 of the file pip selects for the client base, and `environment/Dockerfile` installs it with `--no-deps --require-hashes`, so a build installs exactly those files or fails. The installed packages are the same files as before.

RoboARC 1.1.1, image references moved to ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu (same images, same digests): the Dockerfiles, compose files and README name `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/<image>:<tag>@sha256:<digest>` with the digests of 1.1.0 (images/pins.json). The runtime binding is unchanged, and nothing else changed: results graded under 1.1.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.2.0, three scenes per base (appearance seeds): seed 0 is the released scene, unchanged; seeds 1 and 2 are the same scene and physics in other colours, materials and textures. The task allows seeds 0, 1 and 2 (`[metadata.seeds]`); the runner picks the trial's seed and the image stages that seed's frozen instance against its own runtime binding (`runtime_binding.s<S>.json`, `stage_instance.py --seed-file`). `oracle` lists seed 0 and the seeds whose Harbor oracle run passed; the reference serves every seed (re-stamped with each seed's birth where it records one). Image `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/roboarc:1.2.0` (the seeds' simulator source and tooling); seed 0's birth, end state and render inputs are those of 1.1.x, so results graded under 1.1.x stand.

RoboARC 1.2.1, the renderer checks the GPU before it starts: `nyx_direct.py` reads the Vulkan extensions of the task's GPU and, where `VK_KHR_ray_query` is missing (GPUs without RT cores, such as V100, A100 and H100), raises `nyx_direct.UnsupportedDevice` naming what is missing, instead of letting the native renderer crash the process. There the privileged verifier grades without its replay video (`video_rendered` 0) and the agent's camera calls raise an error it can catch; standard mode needs a GPU with RT cores. On a GPU with RT cores nothing changes. The runtime binding names the new `nyx_direct.py`; the image, the instruction, the grader, the simulator tooling, the frozen instance and the reference are unchanged: results graded under 1.2.0 stand.

RoboARC 1.3.0, the simulator source and tooling of a new experimental family (wire_splicing, not in tasks/ until the owner has reviewed it): the family's code, its two opt-in grasp options (welding a wire's links between the pads, holding between the pads) and an opt-in weld work guard, which only that family's scene profile turns on. Image `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/roboarc:1.3.0` (simulator source and tooling v22). This task's instance, physics, instruction, grader and reference are unchanged, and so are its birth and end states (seeds 0, 1 and 2): results graded under 1.2.x stand.

RoboARC 2.1.0, image `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/roboarc:2.1.0`: the simulator source draws a card in the five bed-bolt scenes (visual only), fixes a crash in wire_splicing's coil count on a straight tail, and lets the blanket families' release check leave out the world-fixed arm bases (see those tasks' own entries); the buzz-wire 06, 07 and 10 texts state their own loop opening. Unless this task's own entry says otherwise, its instance, physics, instruction, grader and reference are unchanged, and so are its birth and end states (seeds 0, 1 and 2): results graded under 2.0.0 stand.

RoboARC 2.2.0, image `ghcr.io/mll-lab-nu/roboarc:2.2.0`: appearance seeds v2. Seeds 1 and 2 change the room's lighting, the table top's material, the table's frame and the floor, and the task's objects' colours and finishes; they are other scenes than the seeds 1 and 2 of 1.2.0-2.1.0, so results at those seeds (and aggregates over a task's seeds) are not comparable with earlier ones. Seed 0 looks and reads as in 2.1.0 unless this task's own entry says otherwise. The physics, the graders, the births and the reference rows are unchanged at every seed: results graded under 2.1.0 stand.

Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. A hold that breaks (the fingers open more than 15 %, the part drifts 1 cm / 0.15 rad from its held pose, the hold has to push or pull its part with more than 65 N averaged over 20 ms, or no finger has touched the part for 0.2 s) is lost, and the gripper must open before it can take hold again; that force is reached when, for example, two held parts that hook into each other are pulled apart, or a held part is pressed into another object. Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. slotted-post-ring-04-i01.grasp_rules: assisted grasping (contact_weld_v1): a gripper whose command moves towards closed takes hold of a graspable part (slotted_chain) once both fingers touch the same part inside its grasp region, the tool frame within 9 cm of it and the penetration at most 2 mm, for 0.02 s; the part then follows the gripper rigidly. Any command that opens the gripper (by more than 0.2 % of its travel) lets it go. A hold that breaks (the fingers open more than 15 %, the part drifts 1 cm / 0.15 rad from its held pose, or the hold has to push or pull its part with more than 60 N averaged over 20 ms) is lost, and the gripper must open before it can take hold again; that force is reached when, for example, two held parts that hook into each other are pulled apart, or a held part is pressed into another object. Two grippers never hold the same part; other objects are grasped physically (friction)
slotted-post-ring-04-i01.grasp: assisted (his contact_weld_v1 grasp regions on slotted_chain)

grasp_regions.privileged: Grasp regions (assisted grasping, see Grippers above; one sphere per graspable part): slotted_chain: radius 77.5 mm. Both finger contacts must lie inside the part's sphere; a part touched elsewhere is grasped physically. Each region's centre (in its link's frame) is in `/app/instance.json` under `simulator.grasp_assist.targets`.
